title: You Just Went Back Before Kyoto
intro: Nara held the capital before Kyoto did.
task: Find one thing that feels older than Gion: a hall, a statue, a tree.
reveal: The capital sat here first. Then it moved.

title: Why Are There Deer Everywhere?
intro: Watch the deer. Why would a city let them walk the park?
task: Watch the deer. Why would a city let them walk the park?
reveal: They are treated as messengers of Kasuga. Sacred status is cultural, not a zoo rule.

title: Do Deer Really Bow?
intro: Watch several deer, not one. Do they bow without food?
task: Watch several deer, not one. Do they bow without food?
reveal: A dip of the head is often a learned ask for biscuits, not a court bow.

title: How Big Can Buddha Get?
intro: Walk in before you look at a photo. How big is the Buddha, in your body: taller than Dad? Taller than the hall?
task: Walk in before you look at a photo. How big is the Buddha, in your body: taller than Dad? Taller than the hall?

moreInfo.title: State and faith
moreInfo.text: A huge Buddha is prayer and politics: a ruler showing care and power. Confirm the Nara-period framing before live.
moreInfo.audioText: A hall this size is not only faith. It is also a state saying: we can build this. Check the emperor and the date before this page is live.
